items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1961-01-29
items.q: And, uh, the saxophone section was, uh, uh, let's see, Willie, uh, Willie Humphrey was in there playing, I think, third sax.

ctx.x: And when did you go after this band broke up?

Well, as I said, we, we, in Pensacola, we were working for these people, and so, uh, we used to play a town like, like Mobile, and go to Montgomery, and, uh, there's a couple other times we'd go. So, uh, around about, uh, let's see, close to 26, well, we left Pensacola, no, we made a trip down to Florida, that's what we made, a trip all over from Pensacola to, uh, Jacksonville, Florida. Well, this guy, here in the...

he was managing the band and booking the band because they didn't have no bookies no day, but he was a man that knew a lot of people, you see. And we booked this all the way to Jacksonville. We stayed, I remember it was in the winter we were in Jacksonville, Florida. And the fella George Morris, he had been a cook one time. He suggested that we go down to Miami or Panama, way down up in there, you see. And well, the fella, they wasn't doing so good on the road and everybody wanted to get back to Pensacola, you…

items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1959-01-17
items.q: she had requested that we would hire Willie Hump. Albert Nicholas was the one that I remember my dad is he played with him with the Silver Leaf Band

ctx.x: About how old were you? Can we get that?

Well, it's kind of hard. I should have figured it out, but I was in about fourth or fifth grade. Well, you're quite young. At that time, kids were pretty old. I mean, not like now, you know, so I must have been around about 10 or 11 years old, maybe older than that. Because I can wait and bring in this park. I can remember in 1924, I was just about ready to make it. I hadn't quite, I hadn't even made 18 or close to it. And that was April, like I'm born in January. And that was when, of course, I'm going to get to…

Albert Nicholas was the one that I remember my dad is he played with him with the Silver Leaf Band and they use a violin because my dad at one time had a bass violin I don't know whether it was either with long term but sometime maybe on going to those jobs there was three of them mostly like a bass violin a guitar and sometimes they'd use a mandolin what did Albert Nicholas play I believe no I'm not thinking of Albert Nicholas the one that we know now is the clan that played but this guy I believe played was the…

items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1959-01-17
items.q: Willie Humphrey had been in there with Manuel Perez, and Capri, and that same group, they had been again a long time, you see.

ctx.x: Did you ever hear Alonzo Ross? Alonzo Ross. Alonzo Ross, he was a piano player I think over there. From where? Around Jacksonville, I think.

Well, I probably met him, a lot of the guys. He went to New York. Yeah. Well, that happened years later because now I want to get, you still get on that same kick in Jacksonville. Now, Eagle Eyes had came out somewhere and heard our band. In fact, we even went up and sat in with the band. And he liked me, who I played bands, he liked the way Alvin Morgan played the bass, and he liked the way Edmund Hall played his playing and sax. And he wanted us to quit the band. That we had always promised that we would come…
Oh, excuse me. Did you say who the piano player was originally? Emma Barron.

items.q: My father knew the family very well.

Then they started having concerts, you see, the first one, Iowa, was in Japan, yeah, in 19... No, I went somewhere because I was with George Lou's band, yeah. We played some old Cincinnati, and then St. Paul, the Twin Cities, and a couple other…

Uh-huh. Yeah. And like from, you know, when you came back to New Orleans to about, what was that, 45, I mean, 48 to 65? 48, 48. Yeah. You were, you found, you played quite a bit of music in that time, didn't you?
